source_title: Iran war live: Araghchi says talks under way on 2-day plan to reopen Hormuz
source_excerpt: ‘Epic resilience’ by Iran’s military has brought the US and allies to the ‘hard wall of reality’ over the conflict, official says. Iran FM Araghchi calls US dialogue offer ‘a positive step’ as Iranian delegation visits Doha Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine” but claims that he’s “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine” but claims that he’s “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks are ongoing with Qatari mediators on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US cooperates. Tehran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, says a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance changed the US tone “completely” describing it as a “very positive sign”. live-orange 50s ago ( 17:30 GMT ) LISTEN: Will diplomacy work between US and Iran before elections? In a statement shared on X by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the kingdom reiterated its “rejection of all violations that threaten the security and safety of maritime navigation and global energy supplies”. The ministry urged the international community to take immediate action to uphold international law and “ensure maritime security and the safety of international trade”. The Al Mayeda is owned and operated by the Qatar Gas Transport Company, and was struck earlier today in the Gulf. In a statement, GCC Secretary-General Jassim Mohammed al-Budaiwi described the attack on the vessel, operated by Qatar’s Gas Transport Company (Nakilat), as a “dangerous escalation”. He stressed that “maritime security in the Arabian Gulf is a cornerstone of regional stability and the global economy”. Al-Budaiwi warned that targeting gas tankers could disrupt global energy supplies, destabilise markets and damage the marine environment. He also called for those responsible for the “heinous attack” to be held accountable. The GCC reaffirmed its support for Qatar’s measures to safeguard its resources, protect its assets and confront threats to its security and interests. Qashqavi said Araghchi briefed the committee on recent regional and diplomatic developments, including visits to Iran by delegations from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Five police officers were “killed in a horrific massacre committed by the Israeli occupation” on Sunday. We have to remember talks stalled until the Qataris stepped in and helped with Pakistani efforts, leading to the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. That has since collapsed , however. It was interesting to hear Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi talk about how Iran initially had a seven-day plan on the table to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. When the Qataris visited Tehran just a few days ago, they tried to bring it down to five days or less. He’s now saying any possible deal can be implemented within two days. I think that’s significant and shows Iran is very keen on reaching an agreement. There’s a sense in the region that things can escalate extremely quickly, especially with the US midterm elections approaching, and the Israeli elections having just taken place. That creates a sense of urgency to reach a deal. Freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz is extremely important for the Gulf. Oil and gas are the bread and butter of the region’s economies, but they’re also critical to global energy supplies. We’re now seeing the cost of living rise and protests across Europe.
